reply_text:
I found one statement from 2020 that fits your rules, and it's a weak one. It comes from MIT Technology Review's feature on AGI, published 15 October 2020 and written by Will Douglas Heaven. In it Legg is quoted saying: "But if we keep moving quickly, who knows?… In a few decades' time, we might have some very, very capable systems." The time span is "a few decades", and the claim is hedged with "might". The only source is a journalist's article, not Legg's own words or a printed interview, and the article doesn't say when he spoke to the reporter.

Nothing else turned up from 2020. The rest of what he said in that article looks back at the past, so it doesn't count. Search results showed a Spotify listing for "The Arrival of AGI" dated Jan 17, 2020, but the episode itself is from December 2025, so I treated the 2020 date as a listing error. I didn't open that page. I found no 2020 podcast, talk, essay or post by Legg with a dated prediction. His well-known "50% chance of AGI by 2028" forecast shows up in other years only: in a 2021 tweet, in 2023 interviews and in 2025 posts. I used 9 of 12 searches and 1 of 6 page openings.
